findings.headline: Sundry debt outstanding at 30 September 2026 is £43.1m, of which £20.105m is over 365 days old.
findings.detail: The paper says £28.5m of the outstanding debt relates to Adults & Housing, including deferred payment and gross without prejudice debts. Collectable debt is £29.4m. Of the prior-year arrears of £44.32m, £28.7m (65%) has been recovered.
findings.matters: The age profile and the share of arrears recovered show how much of a council's receivables are at risk of write-off.
findings.figures: £43.1m sundry debt outstanding; £20.105m over 365 days; £28.5m Adults & Housing; £29.4m collectable debt; £44.32m prior-year arrears; £28.7m (65%) recovered
findings.quote: the balance of sundry debt outstanding at 30 September 2026 was £43.1m

findings.headline: Council tax collection is at 55.62% at 30 September 2026, against 55.87% at the same point last year.
findings.detail: The paper says council tax debt raised in 2026/27 is £455.3m, of which £253.3m has been collected. The paper notes the fall equates to approximately £1.1m less collected in cash terms. Business rates collection rose to 60.24% from 58.72%.
findings.matters: Council tax collection rate is a standard lender measure of the council tax base's cash health, and a fall year on year is one peers track.
findings.figures: 55.62% collection rate; 55.87% prior year; £455.3m council tax debt raised; £253.3m collected; approximately £1.1m less collected; 60.24% business rates collection (58.72% prior year)
findings.quote: The collection rate at 30 September 2026 was 55.62%, compared with 55.87% at the same point in the previous year.

findings.headline: Business rates income is forecast at a £0.543m shortfall, because the budget was set before the NNDR1 return was completed.
findings.detail: The paper says the completed NNDR1 shows lower expected income than originally estimated. This gap is part of the Central Finance overspend.
findings.matters: A budget set before the NNDR1 return was completed is a timing issue that other councils set budgets around each year.
findings.figures: £0.543m business rates shortfall; £0.056m Education Services Grant income; £1.000m LGPS improvement
findings.quote: The current forecast shows a £0.543m shortfall in Business Rates income.

findings.headline: The Waste Collection overspend is now forecast at £0.757m, with fuel pressure of circa £0.650m.
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast worsened since the previous Cabinet report because of vehicle fuel prices. Approximately 75% of the fleet uses HVO fuel, whose price has risen above budget. Fleet partly offsets this with a £0.146m parts underspend.
findings.matters: Fuel price exposure in a waste collection fleet is a cost pressure that many councils have, so the mitigation of partial HVO use is a comparison point.
findings.figures: £0.757m Waste Collection overspend; circa £0.650m fuel pressure; approximately 75% of DC fleet on HVO; £0.146m Fleet parts underspend
findings.quote: The projected overspend is now at £0.757m in Waste Collection.

findings.headline: Dorset Travel is projecting a £1.752m underspend, while SEND transport contracts for September 2026 are assessed at circa £2.2m below budget.
findings.detail: The paper says SEND transport expenditure is forecast at £22,253k for 2026/27, up £2,029k or 10% on 2025/26. Mainstream school transport contract prices are circa £0.5m below budget. Public transport concessionary fares are forecast circa £1m adverse.
findings.matters: SEND transport is one of the most volatile budget lines, and a finance director elsewhere will recognise the pattern of rising cost and then contract renewals coming in below budget.
findings.figures: £1.752m Dorset Travel underspend; circa £44m net budget; circa £2.2m SEND transport below budget; £22,253k 2026/27 SEND transport forecast; £2,029k (10%) increase; circa £0.5m mainstream transport below budget; circa £1m concessionary fares adverse
findings.quote: Now that the majority of contract changes for September 2026 have been assessed, these have been assessed as being circa £2.2m below the budget.

findings.headline: Bridport Connect demolition total project cost is £662,109, against an original demolition budget of £179,280, and £482,829 is requested from the Capital Contingency Fund.
findings.detail: The paper says asbestos discoveries from May 2026 and further contamination found in August 2026 drove the increase. Demolition was brought forward after the redevelopment procurement failed and the vacant building suffered break-ins and arson.
findings.matters: A capital scheme whose cost roughly quadruples from its original budget, with a draw on contingency, shows how site condition risk can move a project's cost.
findings.figures: £179,280 original demolition budget; £257,829 asbestos removal increase; £225,000 further remediation estimate; £662,109 total project cost; £482,829 additional from Capital Contingency
findings.quote: The original demolition budget was £179,280, however, the asbestos removal increased costs initially by £257,829 and the latest estimates require a further £225,000 bringing the total project costs to £662,109.

findings.headline: Capital programme expenditure and commitments total £52.144m (49%) of the £106.025m approved programme at 30 September 2026.
findings.detail: The paper says the programme includes 78 projects. Economy & Environment has 54 projects with £87.248m budget and 52% spent. Core Services is at 13%. Reprofiling of £8.441m moved budget into future years.
findings.matters: A low spend ratio at mid-year shows how much of the programme is at risk of further reprofiling, which is a pattern a peer council can compare.
findings.figures: £106.025m approved programme; £52.144m spent and committed (49%); 78 projects; £8.441m reprofiled; Core Services 13% spent
findings.quote: As at 30 September 2026, expenditure and commitments against the approved capital programme of £106.025m totalled £52.144m (49%).

findings.headline: £8.0m is anticipated to be drawn from reserves to meet the projected overspend, with the General Fund forecast at £40.7m at year-end.
findings.detail: The paper says the General Fund balance was £35.9m at the end of 2025/26 and is forecast to rise to £40.7m. Earmarked reserves were £120m at the end of 2025/26, with a similar balance expected at March 2027.
findings.matters: A forecast draw of this size from reserves tests how much cover remains for the next year's budget and for DSG risk.
findings.figures: £8.0m drawdown from reserves; £35.9m General Fund at end of 2025/26; £40.7m General Fund forecast at end of 2026/27; £120m earmarked reserves at end of 2025/26; approximately £161m total reserves at 31 March 2027
findings.quote: Based on the current revenue forecast, it is anticipated that £8.0m will need to be drawn from reserves to meet the projected overspend.

findings.headline: Dorset’s SEND Reform plan was accepted by government, which the paper describes as a key milestone in securing a 90% write-off of the cumulative DSG overspend.
findings.detail: The paper says a High Needs Stability Grant of £145m is due in November 2026, leaving £3.7m to be funded from the Safety Valve reserve. It also says the long-term SEND reforms have yet to be finalised by government.
findings.matters: Government acceptance of a SEND reform plan tied to a write-off is the mechanism other councils with DSG deficits are waiting on.
findings.figures: 90% write-off of cumulative DSG overspend; £145m High Needs Stability Grant due November 2026; £3.7m balance from the Safety Valve reserve; £148.7m cumulative deficit
findings.quote: Dorset’s SEND Reform plan was accepted by government, which is a key milestone in securing a 90% write off of the cumulative DSG overspend.

findings.headline: The DSG overspend is forecast at £74.3m in 2026/27, and the cumulative deficit is forecast at approximately £150m by 31 March 2028.
findings.detail: The cumulative DSG deficit was £148.7m at 31 March 2026. The paper says the statutory override runs to March 2028 and that the deficit costs circa £6m in interest foregone. The paper also lists EHCP numbers at around 5,000, up from 1,407 in 2013.
findings.matters: A DSG deficit held off the balance sheet by the statutory override is a liability a finance director must track even though it does not show in the general fund.
findings.figures: £74.3m DSG overspend in 2026/27; £148.7m cumulative deficit at 31 March 2026; approximately £150m forecast at 31 March 2028; £6m interest foregone; around 5,000 EHCPs (1,407 in 2013)
findings.quote: Dorset's DSG deficit is forecast to be approximately £150m by 31 March 2028.

findings.headline: Capital financing is forecast at a £1.403m underspend, driven by a £1.863m reduction in forecast interest payable.
findings.detail: The paper says the reduction in interest payable is partly offset by a £1.460m reduction in forecast interest receivable. The underspend is £0.403m better than at Q1.
findings.matters: Interest payable and receivable both moving down is a direct read on the council's borrowing and cash position, which lenders and peers follow closely.
findings.figures: £1.403m underspend; £1.863m reduction in interest payable; £1.460m reduction in interest receivable; £0.403m improvement since Q1
findings.quote: The improved position is driven by a £1.863m reduction in forecast interest payable, partially offset by a £1.460m reduction in forecast interest receivable.

findings.headline: Children's Services is forecast at a £2.3m overspend, an improvement of £0.7m since P4.
findings.detail: The paper says the forecast remains highly sensitive to placement activity. Recruitment challenges and vacancies are partly offsetting the children in care overspend. A Dorset Children Thrive savings programme is included in the Director's Services underspend.
findings.matters: A directorate reducing its overspend mid-year while placement activity stays sensitive shows the trend a finance director would want to track.
findings.figures: £2.3m overspend (2.2%); £0.7m improvement since P4; £106.2m net budget; £108.5m forecast outturn
findings.quote: Overall, the Children's Services Directorate is forecasting a net overspend of £2.3m, an improved position of £0.7m since P4.

findings.headline: Children in Care placements are forecast at £4.6m overspent, of which external homes account for £6.4m.
findings.detail: The paper says external residential placement numbers have risen to 54 from 44 in April 2025, at an average weekly cost of £6,825. It says the external residential market is not functioning effectively and that fostering provision is holding steady at 219 children.
findings.matters: A widening gap between external residential costs and in-house provision is a pattern many councils face when external placement markets tighten.
findings.figures: £4.6m placements overspend (£4.6m at P4); £6.4m external homes overspend; 54 external residential placements; £6,825 average weekly external residential cost; 451 children in care; £2.0m estimated annual cost of the growth above 475 children
findings.quote: The Children in Care placements budget is currently forecast to overspend by £4.6m (£4.6m in P4), this includes fostering and in house residential provision.

findings.headline: Adult Social Care packages are forecast at £4.446m overspent, while the Adult Care Operation is forecast at £1.147m underspent.
findings.detail: The paper says vacancy factor savings are delivering 68% of the directorate's vacancy target and are expected to exceed it. Health funding pressures from jointly funded and CHC cases handed back to the council are estimated at £0.924m.
findings.matters: Health funding that moves back to the council is a cost pressure that the paper calls hard to predict, and it is a pattern other councils will face.
findings.figures: £4.446m packages overspend; £1.147m operation underspend; 68% of vacancy target delivered; £0.924m health funding pressure; £0.176m increase since Q1
findings.quote: currently estimated at £0.924m, an increase of £0.176m since Q1.

findings.headline: Adult Social Care forecasts a £3.312m overspend, with 4,562 people supported at £935 per week at 1 September against a budget of 4,415 people at £887 per week.
findings.detail: The paper says the overspend is primarily due to demand. The number of people supported has held at 4,562 since Q1, while the average weekly cost rose by a further £11. Additional Q1 contingency of £3.5m was allocated.
findings.matters: Both volume and unit cost are rising above budget, which is the mechanism behind most social care overspends across the sector.
findings.figures: £3.312m overspend; 4,415 budgeted people; 4,562 people at 1 September; £887 budgeted average weekly cost; £935 average weekly cost; £3.5m Q1 contingency
findings.quote: As at 1 September, the number of people being supported had increased to 4,562, while the average weekly cost had risen to £935 per week.

findings.headline: Directorate savings delivery at September 2026 totals £9.0m green, £7.5m amber and £6.2m red against £22.7m of 2026/27 savings.
findings.detail: The paper says savings categorised as red will not be achieved this financial year and explains the financial position. Amber savings are at risk. Central Finance holds the largest red value at £4.283m.
findings.matters: The red and amber split is the most direct measure of how much of a budget's savings plan will not land in the year.
findings.figures: £22,657,093 total savings; £8,984,401 green; £7,452,942 amber; £6,219,750 red; Central Finance red £4,283,000
findings.quote: Savings categorised as ‘red’ will not be achieved this financial year and are a reason for the financial position

findings.headline: Transformation savings are forecast at £3.7m at P6 against a £9.4m budget, with £5.7m still to deliver.
findings.detail: The breakdown is £1.1m from workforce redesign in 2026/27, £2.6m full-year effect from 2025/26 activity, and £1.4m forecast for the second half. The paper notes that the remaining £5.7m has mixed confidence.
findings.matters: The split between delivered and remaining savings shows how much of a transformation programme is still unproven in the current year.
findings.figures: £9.4m total budget; £3.7m forecast at P6; £5.7m remainder; £1.1m workforce redesign; £2.6m full-year effect; £1.4m second-half workforce savings
findings.quote: Current forecasts reflect £5.1m of workforce-related savings, comprising £1.1m delivered through workforce redesign activity during 2026/27

findings.headline: Third-party spend savings are forecast at £0m for 2026/27 against a £4.0m budget.
findings.detail: At P4 the council still expected up to £2.0m of third-party savings in the year. The paper says that as plans matured, confidence reduced and no third-party savings are now in the forecast. Work on contract renegotiation continues.
findings.matters: Procurement-led savings that are dropped from the forecast show how a council's savings plan can shrink during the year, which lenders and peers track.
findings.figures: £4.0m budget; £0m forecast at P6; up to £2.0m expected at P4; £4.0m remainder to deliver
findings.quote: As plans have matured, confidence in achieving those savings within the current financial year has reduced and, as a result, no third-party savings are currently reflected within the forecast position.

findings.headline: Dorset Council is considering reimplementing spend controls, as it did in 2025/26.
findings.detail: The paper says the overspend is broadly the same as P4 and that SLT is considering additional spend controls to limit non-essential expenditure for the rest of the year. It also says that without mitigation the forecast would require use of reserves.
findings.matters: Re-introduced spend controls mid-year are a visible signal of how a council is responding to an overspend, and a peer can benchmark that response.
findings.figures: £8.056m overspend forecast; £8.3m at P4
findings.quote: as per 2025/26, the authority is considering reimplementing spend controls.

findings.headline: Dorset Council forecasts a net revenue overspend of £8.056m (1.7%) against a £466m approved budget at September 2026 (P6).
findings.detail: The forecast is a £0.08m improvement on P4. The paper says the position is driven by demand-led pressures in Adult Social Care and Children's Services and by delayed transformation savings. SLT is considering reimplementing spend controls, as it did in 2025/26.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council can compare a P6 overspend of this size, and the choice to consider spend controls again, against their own in-year position.
findings.figures: £8.056m (1.7%); £466m approved budget; £8.3m at P4; £0.08m improvement from P4
findings.quote: At September (P6), the Council is forecasting a net revenue overspend of £8.056m (1.7%) against the approved budget of £466m.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: The order form for the Barnett Waddingham actuarial services contract is out of date, though services and payments continue.
findings.detail: The auditor found the order form out of date and says the contract may not be formally documented through current agreements. The Fund continues to receive actuarial services and makes payment, and management has agreed to review its contract records.
findings.matters: A finance director at any council can see contract documentation being brought into line with a live supplier arrangement.
findings.quote: Our review identified that the order form is out of date.

findings.headline: The audit fee for 2025-26 is £115,886, made up of a £100,886 scale fee for the Pension Fund audit plus £5,000 for triennial valuation data testing and £10,000 for direct property valuation work.
findings.detail: The fees are exclusive of VAT and out-of-pocket expenses. Non-audit fees are £1,100 for IAS 19 assurance letters for admitted bodies.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another council can compare the fund's audit fee build-up against the scale fee.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: Management agreed to add a £3,978,587k carrying value of promised retirement benefits to the accounts, which the audit found was not disclosed.
findings.detail: The auditor found the carrying value of the actuarial present value of promised retirement benefits had not been disclosed, as required by the CIPFA Code. The sensitivity disclosure has also been updated to reflect the latest triennial valuation report.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see the pension liability figure the fund has now disclosed in its accounts.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: Audit could not obtain the retirement assessment documentation for one benefits sample, which the administrator attributes to a 2006 paper-based case not scanned.
findings.detail: The administrator could not provide the retirement assessment sheet for Sample 4. The auditor says it could not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence for that benefit calculation and payment. Management says paper records have not been used since 2021, when the UPM system was introduced.
findings.matters: A finance officer at another fund can see how a gap in legacy paper records surfaced in benefits testing and how the administrator responded.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: Four of six prior-year recommendations are reported as addressed, while budget monitoring of fund account items is still recorded as a finding.
findings.detail: The auditor reports leavers processing, transfers in recognition, investment classification and the property tenancy schedule as addressed, and the journal recommendation as partially addressed. Management says a budget for fund account items was developed and is now reported quarterly to the Pension Fund Committee, but the auditor says the point remains a finding and has been raised again.
findings.matters: A finance director can see which prior-year audit points have closed and which are still open, including fund-account budget reporting.
findings.quote: A budget for fund account items has been developed

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: FB05 journals can still be posted to the ledger without authorisation, and the auditor has raised this again as a recommendation.
findings.detail: The auditor says journals below £50k were previously posted without authorisation and are now reviewed retrospectively, and journals above £50k require approval before posting. FB05 bank-posting journals are still automatically approved regardless of value. The auditor also notes that the Section 151 Officer has journal posting access, though no journals were posted by that officer during the year. Management says compensatory controls are in place and that the SAP system is being replaced.
findings.matters: A finance director at any council using SAP journal controls can compare how FB05 posting and compensatory approval are being handled.
findings.figures: Journal approval threshold £50k
findings.quote: We recommend that compensatory controls are put in place.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: The Pension Fund moved from Brunel to LPPI on 1 April 2026, and audit queries now go directly to individual fund managers, adding administrative effort for the audit.
findings.detail: Responsibility for pooled assets and audit query responses transferred to LPPI. The auditor now sends requests to each fund manager, which requires direct correspondence and monitoring of responses. In March 2026 the fund divested in full from Brunel's Emerging Markets Equity Fund before the pooling change.
findings.matters: Other councils moving to LPPI or other pools can see the audit-process cost reported for this transition.
findings.quote: The Fund transitioned from Brunel to LPPI with effect from 1 April 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: The audit opinion on the Pension Fund financial statements depends on the council's own audit of the Administering Authority, expected to be completed by end of November.
findings.detail: The auditor says it cannot issue its final opinion on the Pension Fund until the Administering Authority audit is complete, and that this is expected by end of November, ahead of the statutory deadline. It also says it cannot certify the Administering Authority audit until its work on the fund's annual report consistency statement is complete.
findings.matters: A finance officer at a peer council sees that the pension fund opinion is tied to the host council's own audit timetable.
findings.quote: we will be unable to issue our final audit opinion on the Pension Fund financial statements until the audit of the Administering Authority is complete.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: Investments of £60.97m are reclassified from Level 3 to Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy after the fund manager review, with comparative figures adjusted.
findings.detail: Two Level 3 investments totalling £40.58m were confirmed by the fund manager as valued using observable inputs. Management's review of the remaining Level 3 investments identified a further £20.39m, and the disclosure has been corrected.
findings.matters: A finance director at another fund can see how a custodian-based classification review moved a large block of investments between fair value levels, which affects the liquidity disclosure.
findings.figures: £60.97m total misclassification; £40.58m in two investments; further £20.39m identified; prior-year figure of £56.8m reclassified
findings.quote: giving a total misclassification of £60.97m.

findings.headline: £6.673 million of investment valuation differences are left unadjusted at 31 March 2026, with management proposing not to amend the accounts on materiality grounds.
findings.detail: The differences are understatements of Level 2 and 3 investments against fund manager confirmations. The auditor's headline materiality is £81.9 million and its reporting threshold is £4.0 million. The Audit and Governance Committee is asked to confirm agreement through the letter of representation.
findings.matters: A lender or finance director can see the size of the unadjusted misstatement against the auditor's materiality, which sets how much valuation error the fund accepts without restating.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 3 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset County Pension Fund
findings.headline: The audit identified no adjustments affecting the Pension Fund's reported financial position at 31 March 2026, and the auditor expects an unmodified opinion on the financial statements.
findings.detail: The auditor says it has not identified adjustments that impact the reported financial position and that its anticipated opinion on the financial statements will be unmodified. Audit work is described as substantially complete, with final review, the management representation letter and the final statements still outstanding.
findings.matters: A finance director at the council or a peer council can read the 2025-26 fund accounts as free of audit adjustments to net assets, with the remaining steps listed.
findings.figures: Total net assets per final accounts £4,549,495k
findings.quote: We have not identified any adjustments that impact on the Pension Fund’s reported financial position.

findings.headline: Council held one LOBO loan at 30 September 2026, £11.0m at a 4.6% average rate
findings.detail: The paper defines a LOBO as a loan where the lender may propose a higher rate at set dates, with the borrower able to repay without additional cost. The LOBO balance is unchanged from 31 March 2026 in the borrowing table, and the paper does not describe a call or rate proposal in the period.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender tracking LOBO exposure across the sector needs to know whether a loan remains held after the period in which lenders could propose rate changes.
findings.figures: Banks (LOBO) £11.0m at 30 September 2026, average rate 4.6%, average maturity 50.6 years
findings.quote: At 30 September 2026, the Council held one such loan.

findings.headline: External borrowing fell £12m in the six months to 30 September 2026, to £303m
findings.detail: The paper attributes the net decrease to the Council's strategy for funding previous and current years' capital programmes. Public Works Loan Board borrowing fell by £16.3m in the period, while short-term local authority borrowing rose by £5.0m.
findings.matters: A mid-year reduction in debt, combined with a shift in lender mix, is the kind of movement a lender or finance director tracks against the full-year forecast.
findings.figures: External borrowing £315m at 31 March 2026 reduced to £303m at 30 September 2026 (net decrease £12m); PWLB net movement £-16.3m; short-term local authority borrowing £55.0m to £60.0m
findings.quote: held £303m of loans, a net decrease of £12m from 31 March 2026

findings.headline: Capital Financing Requirement forecast at £490m by 31 March 2027, £4m below budget due to slippage in the capital programme
findings.detail: The CFR is forecast to rise from £449m at the start of the year, which is slightly less than budgeted because of slippage in delivering the capital programme.
findings.matters: Slippage that lowers the CFR below budget is a signal of delivery pace that finance directors and lenders track alongside borrowing plans.
findings.figures: CFR £449m at 31 March 2026; forecast £490m at 31 March 2027 vs £494m budget
findings.quote: £4 million below budget due to slippage in the capital programme

findings.headline: Final redemption of legacy strategic pooled property funds leaves the Council with no long-term strategic pooled fund investments, down from £1.3m at 31 March 2026
findings.detail: Proceeds from the redemption were received in September 2026. The paper says the Council prefers to use balance sheet resources to reduce the need for external borrowing rather than hold strategic pooled funds.
findings.matters: Exiting inherited property fund holdings removes a source of price volatility and shows an explicit choice to use balance sheet resources to reduce external borrowing.
findings.figures: Property funds £1.3m at 31 March 2026 reduced to £0.0m at 30 September 2026
findings.quote: meaning the Council no longer holds long-term strategic pooled fund investments.

findings.headline: All treasury management activity in the six months to 30 September 2026 complied with the limits and parameters in the 2026/27 Treasury Management Strategy
findings.detail: The paper reports compliance with the CIPFA Code and the approved strategy, and says the Council's authorised limit and operational boundary for external debt were both met. Total external debt was £333m against an operational boundary of £510m and an authorised limit of £535m.
findings.matters: Confirmed compliance with prudential limits at mid-year is a basic assurance a lender or peer finance team checks.
findings.figures: Total external debt £333m at 30 September 2026; operational boundary £510m; authorised limit £535m
findings.quote: All treasury management activity in the year to 30 September 2026 complied with the limits and parameters included in the Treasury Management Strategy for 2026/27

findings.headline: The need for external borrowing is expected to rise again in 2027/28, with the liability benchmark showing £405m at 31 March 2028 and £490m at 31 March 2029
findings.detail: The paper says reductions in balance sheet resources, primarily driven by continuing annual SEND deficits, will meet an increasing loans CFR driven by the unfunded element of the capital programme. It says this will need to be considered as part of 2027/28 budget setting.
findings.matters: A forecast return to rising external borrowing after a year of falling debt is a key signal for lenders and for finance officers at councils with continuing SEND deficits.
findings.figures: Liability benchmark external borrowing £405m at 31 March 2028 and £490m at 31 March 2029; balance sheet resources £195m forecast at 31 March 2027 falling to £115m at 31 March 2028 and £35m at 31 March 2029
findings.quote: the need for external borrowing is expected to rise again in 2027/28

findings.headline: Internal borrowing forecast to rise from £107m to £160m by 31 March 2027, £60m more than budget

findings.matters: A forecast £60m below budget on external debt is a large variance that a finance director or lender would want to see explained.

findings.matters: Councils facing structural change would want to know how auditors are treating going concern when a council's current form may end, and lenders would want to see the basis for that judgement.

findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders would want to see how a council reports and assesses the effect of fraud investigations on its accounts.

findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, would want to know whether a 2025/26 audit is at risk of a qualified opinion or disclaimer because of missing evidence on asset and reserve balances.

findings.detail: The understatement arose from the need to complete pension fund accounts by the statutory deadline. The paper also records a prior-year unadjusted timing difference of £1,480k, bringing the cumulative unadjusted effect to £2,342k on the net defined benefit liability.
findings.matters: A pension fund valuation error caused by deadline pressure shows how the statutory timetable can affect balances that councils and lenders rely on.

findings.matters: A clean-up of the fixed asset register that removes stale depreciated assets is a concrete step other councils with unverified asset registers can compare their own progress against.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Audit Findings Report (ISA260) 2025-26 - Dorset Council
findings.headline: Journal entries below £50k are automatically self-approved, and the auditor says the council's new manual review control does not fully mitigate the risk.
findings.detail: The paper cites a lack of second user authorisation and no automated process to show that the review took place in SAP. The auditor tested 60 journals this year, down from 80 in the prior year, and found no issues in that sample.
findings.matters: Automatic self-approval of journals in SAP is a control weakness that peer councils running similar finance systems would check in their own audits.

findings.headline: Inconsistencies in car park valuation calculations overstated the valuation by £2.5 million, and the valuer reworked the calculations for all car parks.
findings.detail: The auditor also found a £600k understatement from an incorrect rental income figure and a £225k understatement from conversion works. These were not adjusted because they are immaterial, and the auditor has raised a recommendation on the valuation process.
findings.matters: Property valuation errors on a large asset base are a common source of audit risk, and the rework and recommendation show the control gap that other councils with similar portfolios would check.

findings.headline: £30.9 million of social care and Better Care Fund grant was reclassified from non-specific grant income into cost of services, with a prior period adjustment of a similar amount.
findings.detail: The auditor found that the grants carry restrictions on use, so they belong in service income rather than taxation and non-specific grant income. The same misclassification existed in the prior year, so a prior period adjustment was made.

findings.headline: Debtors and creditors were each overstated by £24.7 million through a prepayment linked to Care Dorset Ltd, and this was adjusted in the accounts.
findings.detail: The purchase order related to 2026/27 services that had not been received at year end. The related party note was also corrected, reducing Care Dorset Ltd turnover from £48.7 million to £32.5 million because it had included 18 months of transactions.
findings.matters: A large year-end prepayment from an arm's-length company error shows how a purchasing control gap can overstate both sides of the balance sheet, which is a useful check for finance officers at peer councils.

findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion on a council's accounts, driven by the backstop regime, is a key signal to lenders and to finance directors at other councils working through the same local audit recovery.

findings.paper_title: 2026-11-10 MTFP and budget report to Cabinet

It also says that if the override ends without a full write-off, many Section 151 officers across England would be considering a section 114 notice.

findings.headline: Governance maturity risk rating improved from high to medium between June and October 2026, as portfolio moved from design to implementation phase.
findings.detail: The council's assessment of governance maturity improved from high risk in June 2026 to medium risk in October 2026, driven by establishment of clearer senior leadership accountability, strengthened Transformation Board, maturing Design Authority arrangements, critical path reviews and more structured benefits oversight. The overall portfolio remains high risk, but the nature of risk has evolved: uncertainty regarding organisational direction and governance has reduced, with risk now increasingly concentrated on delivery, organisational capacity, benefits realisation, ERP implementation, data readiness and service stabilisation.
findings.matters: The shift from governance uncertainty to implementation risk signals the council has resolved directional questions but must now execute complex interdependent delivery; this is a material change in what can go wrong.

findings.headline: Cumulative DSG deficit of £148.7m kept off council's balance sheet via statutory override extended to March 2028, but creating £4.9m annual cashflow pressure.

findings.matters: A material off-balance-sheet deficit affecting council cash availability and requiring General Fund subsidy is a key financial risk that lenders and peer councils monitor closely.

findings.quote: Premises Related Costs 48,000 111,569 (63,569) (A)

findings.paper_title: Budget Monitoring App 1- Bridport Financial Summary 2026-27
findings.headline: Fees and charges income forecast at £751,076 against budget of £794,600, a shortfall of £43,524.
findings.detail: Harbour fee income is running 5.5% below budget. The paper provides no explanation for the shortfall, which could indicate lower than expected harbour activity, service disruption, or demand pressure. This is a material variance given that fees are the largest revenue item for the service.
findings.matters: Income volatility in a user-fee-funded service signals revenue risk to a lender and indicates whether the service is demand-dependent and potentially vulnerable to external shocks.
findings.figures: Fees and Charges budgeted £794,600, forecast £751,076, adverse variance £43,524.

findings.paper_title: Budget Monitoring App 1- Bridport Financial Summary 2026-27
findings.headline: Harbour revenue surplus forecast at £71,807 against £90,400 budgeted, an adverse variance of £18,593.
findings.detail: The shortfall in operating surplus is driven by fees and charges running £43,524 below budget (forecast £751,076 vs budget £794,600) and premises costs overrunning by £63,569 (forecast £111,569 vs budget £48,000). These are partially offset by pay cost savings of £24,000 and supplies savings of £30,000. The reduced surplus constrains the service's ability to self-fund capital and maintenance spending.
